title: scheduler: lease probe coordinator and adaptive timeout for continuous batcher
author: Evan Park
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher fairness and starvation resilience: introduces a lease probe coordinator and per-queue adaptive timeouts to reduce p99 latency spikes under KV-heavy workloads.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed intermittent p99 latency spikes in the continuous batcher when a small subset of requests (KV-heavy, long-generation) would pin worker shards and starve other queues for extended periods. This PR implements a lightweight lease-probe coordinator plus an adaptive timeout policy per queue to detect and recover from soft-starvation without jeopardizing throughput.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Adds a lease-probe coordinator that periodically probes long-held queue leases to detect stalls and recommend lease relinquish/backoff.
- Implements an adaptive timeout estimator per logical queue (based on recent completion quantiles) to bound how long a lease can be held before the coordinator intervenes.
- Integrates probe signals with the existing batching admission controller so the batcher can preemptively rebalance when KV-pin metrics indicate disproportionate cache usage.
- Exposes two new runtime knobs: scheduler.lease_probe_interval and scheduler.adaptive_timeout_multiplier (both configurable via server config).
- Includes unit and integration tests, plus a perf canary harness that reproduces the KV-heavy starvation mode.

Small illustrative snippet (from timeout_estimator.rs):
"""
// estimate the 95th completion latency and multiply by factor to set the soft lease limit
let recent_p95 = hist.quantile(0.95);
let soft_limit_ms = (recent_p95 as f64 * config.adaptive_timeout_multiplier) as u64;
"""

Performance impact (canary):
- Baseline (before): p50=12ms, p95=78ms, p99=420ms under KV-burst mix
- With PR: p50=12ms, p95=72ms, p99=160ms (roughly 62% reduction in p99 spikes in reproduced scenario)
- CPU/GPU throughput unchanged within noise (<=2% variance)

Merge notes: Squash-merged to main. Rollout plan: feature gated behind scheduler.enable_lease_probe (default true) and monitored via new metric scheduler.probe.interventions_total and scheduler.queue.adaptive_timeout_ms (exposed in console). Ops run a staged rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours; no regressions observed during canary window.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Add a probabilistic probe backoff to reduce coordinator traffic in very large clusters.
- Explore kernel-level cooperative preemption for long-running GPU-bound generations.
- Tune default adaptive_timeout_multiplier per model family using historical traces.
